beats: This turkey is still frozen. Drop it in hot oil, and the pot erupts.
The fire doesn't start with the oil. It starts with hidden ice.
Frying oil runs at about one hundred eighty Celsius, three hundred fifty Fahrenheit.
Water boils at one hundred Celsius. That oil is almost twice as hot.
A frozen turkey hides ice in its skin and deep inside its cavity.
When that ice hits the oil, it melts and boils almost instantly.
One cup of water makes about seventeen hundred cups of steam.
All that steam forms under the oil and has to push its way up.
The bubbles lift the oil like a piston, and it foams over the rim.
Hot oil runs down the sides, straight onto the burner's open flame.
It ignites, and a pot of burning oil becomes a fireball.
So the fireball doesn't come from the oil. It comes from the water hiding in the bird.
Cogwise: how things work. Follow for the next one!
